simple.meaning: יְנִיקָה (yᵉnîyqâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a sucker or sapling.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יְנִיקָה (H3242) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יְנִיקָה (H3242) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יְנִיקָה (yᵉnîyqâh) / H3242 is traced through Ezekiel 17:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H3242. yeniqah [ יְנִיקָה ] noun feminine id., only plural suffix יְנִיקוֺתָיו Ezek 17:4 of Israel under figure of cedar. יַנְשׁוֺף יַנְשׁוּף, see below נשׁף .

occurrences.englishText: He cropped off the topmost of its young twigs, and carried it to a land of traffic. He planted it in a city of merchants.
